llm.summary: This skill is a local travel-safety lookup tool with no evidence of data collection, network access, persistence, or hidden behavior.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is destination safety lookup, ranking, and comparison; the Python script implements those functions using hard-coded local destination data.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md tool declarations match the script commands and parameters, and the instructions disclose that the data is local and advisory only.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains only SKILL.md, a VERSION file, and one executable Python helper; no install hooks or package-manager scripts were found. The VERSION file says 1.0.2 while metadata says 1.0.3, which is a minor consistency issue rather than a security concern.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The script imports only json and sys, reads command-line arguments, and prints results; no network, filesystem reads beyond its own code, subprocesses, credentials, or environment access were observed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No persistence, privilege escalation, credential/session handling, background worker, or local profile access is present.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Installers should understand this is an offline reference tool with hard-coded, non-real-time safety ratings. It appears safe from a code/security perspective, but users should still check current official travel advisories before relying on its destination guidance.
llm.findings:
[SkillSpector clean] expected: SkillSpector reported no issues; source review supports that conclusion, with the executable script limited to local lookup and formatting.
[Static scan clean] expected: Static scan reported no findings, and manual inspection found no hidden commands, writes, network calls, or unsafe execution paths.
[VirusTotal clean] expected: VirusTotal telemetry showed no malicious or suspicious engine detections; this was treated as supporting telemetry, not the sole basis for the verdict.
